name: Nonuya
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Nonuya appears to have contrastive pitch similar to Ocaina (Orjuela Salinas 2010). Ascending and descending tones regularly tend to co-occur with lengthened vowels. Hyman (2016: 236) places “Huitoto” (Murui-Muina) within “other tonal systems” with a question mark. Wetzels and Meira (2010: 345–346), based on Aschmann’s (1993) data, tentatively hypothesize that Ocaina is a “non-stress [i.e., pitch] accent language”. At present, we suggest that Ocaina, Nonuya, and the Mɨnɨka and Nɨpode dialects of Murui-Muina may be typologized as pitch-accent languages (cf. Hyman 2016: 241, 247).
new_statements.citation: Echeverri, Juan Alvaro; Fagua Rincón, Doris; Wojtylak, Katarzyna I. (submitted version 2023-08-20; forthcoming, repository date 2027). The Witotoan language family. In: International Handbook of Amazonian Languages. Berlin. §2.3 Prosody.
new_statements.locator: §2.3 Prosody, printed p. 10 (PDF p. 11); cf. §3.1 pp. 10-11 and Conclusions p. 66
new_statements.rule_in_words: No fixed stress position is described. The specialists treat Nonuya as having contrastive pitch (two tonal distinctions: high vs low level tones, plus rising and falling contours that co-occur with long vowels or vowel sequences separated by glottal stop) and tentatively typologize it as a pitch-accent language like Ocaina. The only explicit remark on stress is Wojtylak (2016: 7): 'Complex rules of stress assignment (there are no unified stress patterns across Witotoan languages)'; Echeverri & Romero (2016: 148) mention implosives surfacing as [b d] 'en sílabas no acentuadas', so a stressed/unstressed distinction is assumed but its placement is never stated. Orjuela (2010: 44) explicitly leaves 'fenómenos de acentuación' for future study.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the database (Echeverri 2020) notes item-level variation of the 'patrón acentual' between repetitions of the same word (e.g. MR.081-082 hotʲáme ~ /jótame/ 'mi tío').
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, citation forms from elicited word lists and simple sentences of the last four speakers (recordings 1973-2007). The source is a family-overview chapter (submitted version, 'subject to changes') co-written by the primary documenter; its tonal claim rests on Orjuela's 2010 acoustic report and on Romero Cruz 2015a. All sources hedge ('appears', 'may be typologized'); tone marking in the transcriptions is partial (Romero 2015a: 82).
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the same variety: the Nonuya (autonym Nononotá) of the People of the Centre, documented from the last four speakers (Mamerto Ríos, Humberto Ayarce, Rafael Grande, Margarita Kapojó; recordings 1973-2007) for the revitalizing community of Peña Roja, río Caquetá, Colombia; no dialect split. Glottocode nonu1241; language is dormant.

sources.locator: §2.3 Prosody, printed p. 10 (PDF p. 11); cf. §3.1 pp. 10-11 and Conclusions p. 66
sources.note: §2.3 Prosody (p. 10): Nonuya 'appears to have contrastive pitch similar to Ocaina (Orjuela Salinas 2010)'; rising and falling tones co-occur with lengthened vowels; authors 'suggest that Ocaina, Nonuya, and the Mɨnɨka and Nɨpode dialects of Murui-Muina may be typologized as pitch-accent languages'. §3.1 (pp. 10-11): morphemes realised as suprasegmentals, 'accent (Murui-Muina, Ocaina, Nonuya)'. Conclusion p. 66 repeats 'appear to have pitch-accent systems'. No placement rule for stress.

sources.citation: Wojtylak, Katarzyna I. & Echeverri, Juan Alvaro (2026, accepted ms.). Towards a reconstruction of the pronominal system of Proto-Witotoan from the Northwest Amazon. Journal of Historical Linguistics. 36 pp. University of Warsaw repository item/179059.
sources.note: §2.3 Prosody (p. 5): 'NO [Nonuya] appears to have a pitch accent system similar to that of Ocaina'; different tones in vowel sequences or vowels separated by glottal stop; 'one may consider OC, NO, and the Mn and Np dialects of MM as pitch-accent languages'. p. 2: 'In OC and NO, the acute accent marks tonal contours'. No vowel lengthening in Nonuya (Orjuela 2010: 44).

sources.note: Acoustic-phonetic study of Humberto Ayarce's recordings. Análisis fonético: 'dado que al parecer la lengua hace distinciones tonales' F0 was measured; 'para el caso de los tonos no se realizaron estudios a profundidad' (p. ~43). Recomendaciones (p. 44): future tasks are 'el estudio del patrón tonal de la lengua, así como considerar la posibilidad de encontrar fenómenos de acentuación en la misma' - i.e. stress was not investigated; no statement of stress placement.

sources.citation: Wojtylak, Kasia (2016). Some notes on aspects of Nonuya (Witotoan) grammar. Handout, Language and Culture Research Centre, James Cook University, 7 September 2016, 19 pp.

sources.note: §3.1 Phonology (p. 7): 'Nonuya has two tonal distinctions (similar to Ocaina, but distinct from Witoto)'; 'Complex rules of stress assignment (there are no unified stress patterns across Witotoan languages).' Footnote 15: Witoto Murui and Mɨka have fixed accent; Mɨnɨka/Nɨpode different accent placement possibly tonal. Table 10 (p. 15): Nonuya 'two tones'. No stress placement given.

sources.citation: Echeverri, Juan Álvaro & Romero Cruz, Isabel Victoria (2022). La lengua nonuya: historia y estado actual de su proceso de revitalización. In: Lenguas indígenas de América Latina, Iberoamericana Vervuert, pp. 171-184. doi:10.31819/9783968692616-009 (author copy, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.17766189).
sources.note: §4.1 (pp. 183-184) repeats the 2016 text: Nonuya is tonal per Orjuela Salinas (2010), rising/falling tones with vowel lengthening, distinct level tones on geminate or glottal-separated vowels. No statement on stress placement.

sources.citation: Echeverri, Juan Alvaro (2019/2020). Base de datos de la lengua Nonuya, v.4 (8,693 IPA-transcribed records of four speakers, 1973-2007). Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.3899512; and Base de datos Nonuya - grafía normalizada (2020), doi:10.5281/zenodo.14590372.
sources.note: Introduction gives only a phoneme table (adapted from Romero Cruz 2015). Acute accents on vowels mark tonal contour (per Wojtylak & Echeverri 2026: 2). Item-level observations mention 'patrón acentual' / 'patrón prosódico' variation for individual words (e.g. MR.081-082 hotʲáme ~ /jótame/ 'mi tío') but state no rule.

sources.citation: Moreno (Sika), Eliécer et al. (2017). Un nuevo capítulo en la recuperación de la lengua nonuya: testimonio de una experiencia reciente. Mundo Amazónico 8(2). doi:10.15446/ma.v8n2.67156.
Echeverri, Juan Álvaro & Romero Cruz, Isabel Victoria (2016). Agonía y revitalización de una lengua y un pueblo: los nonuya del Amazonas. Forma y Función 29(2): 135-156. doi:10.15446/fyf.v29n2.60192.
sources.note: Fonología (pp. 147-148): 'Orjuela (2010) afirma que el nonuya es una lengua tonal... se hallaron los tonos ascendente y descendente, los cuales suelen aparecer simultáneamente con un alargamiento vocálico... El tono tiene alcance silábico y tiene estatus fonológico hasta donde lo hemos podido establecer.' Only mention of stress: implosives /ɓ/ /ɗ/ 'se realizan como [b] y [d] en sílabas no acentuadas' (p. 148); no placement rule.

sources.citation: Romero Cruz, Isabel Victoria (2015a). Acompañamiento al proceso de revitalización de la lengua nonuya: un caso de lucha por la supervivencia lingüística. Tesis de maestría en lingüística, Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Bogotá. 93 pp.
sources.note: §4.3.3 Observaciones sobre el tono (p. 74): 'Landaburu y Echeverri (ms. s f.) así como Orjuela (2010) afirman que el nononotá es una lengua tonal'; rising and falling tones with vowel lengthening ([v̌:], [v̂:]) and distinct level tones on geminate vowels or vowels separated by [ʔ], with examples (nò.nó:.tɨ̀ 'pepa de achiote' vs nò.nò:.tɨ́ 'mojojoy'). Orthography proposal (p. 84) marks high, low, rising, falling tones. Nothing on stress placement; 'acento' appears only for other Witotoan varieties (p. 44).

sources.citation: Romero Cruz, Isabel Victoria (2015b). Lengua nonuya y conservación lingüística: algunas reflexiones. Mundo Amazónico 6(2): 49-65. doi:10.15446/ma.v6n2.52401.
sources.note: Sociolinguistic essay; no phonology, nothing on stress.
